newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PORTUGUESE SHARES END OFF LOWS, DEPEND ON WALL ST.
newsitem.headline: PORTUGUESE SHARES END OFF LOWS, DEPEND ON WALL ST.

text.p: Portuguese shares ended off the lows after a weak start to the session caused by the pessimistic mood on Wall Street, led by fears over a possible rise in U.S. short term rates. Only Banco Mello resisted the overall downward swing as it benefited from its strong first half results.
* Credit Lyonnais Portugal (CLP), the local unit of French state controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, said it had agreed to sell its retail network to Spanish bank Caixa da Galicia.
A statement said CLP would continue its activities in the large companies and capital market in Portugal.
Earlier, Portugal's Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) suspended trade in CLP.
* Dealers said the opening on Lisbon bourse on Monday would depend on the close of Wall Street today and the early mood in Europe.
